source.title: Towards Vector-Mediated Circuits for Refusal and Sycophancy

record.file_problem: Only abstract/summary text is supplied; the full paper is not present.
record.tranche_reason: It uses direction-conditioned circuit discovery and circuit ablation, rather than the original all-layer, all-position direction ablation, and reports refusal outcomes relevant to whether the coordinate is causally important.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal-circuit reconstruction metrics and refusal behavior when the circuit is retained or ablated. Sycophancy intervention results are omitted because they concern a different behavior, not refusal.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Arditi difference-in-means refusal direction as the target for circuit discovery. It reports its own method's results: how well a 1,000-edge circuit reconstructs the coordinate, and refusal when that circuit is kept or ablated. It does not ablate or add the direction itself. The authors say mediation of behavior by the coordinate is untested: 'scope-matched tests of vector mediation… remain ongoing.' Circuit-ablation effects on refusal concern the circuit, which may act through paths other than the direction, so they do not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as far as it goes. The authors also report that sycophancy has distinct prompt- and response-derived directions with complementary steering effects. They also find natural end-to-end sycophancy far less sparse than trait coordinates. They frame the work as a step toward linking steering directions to circuits, not a complete decomposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive direction extraction but then applies integrated-gradients edge attribution and ablates a 1,000-edge circuit, rather than directly ablating or adding the direction at all layers and positions.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a 1,000-edge circuit found by EAP-IG reconstructs the prompt-level refusal coordinate: 87.8% faithfulness and 100.3% necessity on 64 held-out prompts. On 64 development prompts, retaining only this circuit keeps refusal at 95.3% versus 93.8% normally. Ablating it cuts refusal to 20.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The computation that forms the refusal direction is localized in a compact circuit, and ablating that circuit largely removes refusal.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to the supplied abstract/summary and one model. Refusal evaluation uses 64 development prompts; no uncertainty estimates or controls are reported. Circuit ablation is not the claimed all-position direction ablation, and other abilities are not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: Sycophancy pilot intervention results and sycophancy circuit metrics are omitted because they measure sycophancy rather than refusal.

untested.parts: Direction ablation, direction addition, induced refusal on harmless prompts, and capability preservation are all untested. The authors say vector-mediation tests are ongoing.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text appears to be the whole extended-abstract submission, not just an abstract. It covers one model, n=64 prompts, and no uncertainty or controls. The sycophancy results were rightly left out. Rows were relinked to none because no operation intervenes on the direction itself. If later versions run the planned direction-mediation tests, re-evaluate the study under V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report direct ablation or addition of the difference-in-means direction across all layers and positions, false refusal induced on harmless requests, or effects on general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
No jailbreak suppression of the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conical, or mediated by multiple refusal directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is named; no language or model-stage transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.note: Ablation substantially reduces refusal, but refusal remains; this is circuit ablation, not direct ablation of the direction across all relevant positions.
rows.check: This ablates 1,000 circuit edges, not the refusal direction. The drop from 93.8% to 20.3% is a circuit effect, and the authors say coordinate mediation is not yet tested. The record's 'partial' state against V1 is misapplied.
